besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining two main clauses ('Die Aarde staan ... stil nie' / 'dit reis heeltyd').
besluite.rede: Both clauses have their own subject and verb, so the AWS 2017 comma is required and nothing else changes.

besluite.fout: 'weer uitkom waar dit begin het' is stiff for arriving back at a starting point.
besluite.rede: 'is weer terug waar dit begin het' is the natural Afrikaans phrasing and says the same thing.

besluite.fout: 'die volgende reis' first reads as the noun 'the next journey', especially since 'reis' is a noun throughout the lesson.
besluite.rede: Adding 'een' removes the garden-path reading without changing the meaning.

besluite.fout: 'daardie reis was al tien keer klaar' is illogical and wooden: one journey cannot be finished ten times.
besluite.rede: Saying the Earth has travelled round the Sun ten times by your tenth birthday is natural and keeps the claim exact.

besluite.fout: 'Dit' directly after 'n tweede beweging' can be read as the movement rather than the Earth.
besluite.rede: Naming the Earth fixes an ambiguous pronoun for a Grade 5 reader at the cost of one repeated noun.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma before 'en' joining 'Die Aarde reis om die Son' and 'dit draai om sy eie as'.
besluite.rede: Two main clauses with their own subject and verb take the AWS 2017 comma, consistent with change 1.

Imperative plus 'en' plus result is natural Afrikaans, and splitting it leaves 'Kyk weer in die middel van die dag.' standing alone right after the warning not to look at the Sun, which is a lateral move near safety wording.
